findings.description: `# -fn: overlapping entries snapshot the same link twice.` gives the reason for `-f` (replace the link an earlier entry left) but not for `-n` (don't descend into an existing link-to-directory), so `-n` looks removable. Same line in the .github copy.

The RESTORE_PATHS header invites adding paths the shared tree resolves through, but doesn't mention the new limit: an entry with a link in a leading component (e.g. `.agents/skills/foo` when `.agents/skills` is a link) now fails the review. One clause would head off a confusing failure. Same in the .github copy.

`expect(snapshotDir).toBe(".claude-pr-agents")` hard-codes the literal the test claims to derive from the step, so a rename means editing the test too; `toBeDefined()` would keep the SKILL.md guard (the `toContain` line) without the second edit site.

The SKILL.md-pointer test never runs the restore step; it is a cross-file consistency check and would sit more naturally beside the others in test/workflow-sync.test.ts than in the "workflow's config restore" describe block.
